questions.text: What is the best source-backed reading of topography in site planning?

options.text: Use contours, drainage lines, soil, slope, vegetation, and hazard exposure to shape the site plan.
Treat topography as irrelevant once the lot area is known.
Flatten the site before analyzing drainage.
Use facade style as the main slope criterion.

questions.rationale: Use contours, drainage lines, soil, slope, vegetation, and hazard exposure to shape the site plan. This answer is supported by the checked local raw-source families for Topography and Slope Analysis.

questions.text: Which action best matches the climate-resilience locator?

options.text: Minimize alteration to natural topography and excavation or filling while avoiding increased natural-hazard risk.
Maximize filling to erase natural drainage lines.
Remove vegetation corridors to simplify the grid.
Ignore waterways during lot layout.

questions.explanation: Slope (%) = (Rise/Run) × 100; Ratio = 1:(Run/Rise); θ = arctan(Rise/Run). At 12.5%, moderate grading with standard foundations applies.
